subject: Animation
title: Floyd Norman: Disney's First Black Animator
description: Learn Floyd Norman: Disney's First Black Animator in one minute.

hook.text: Floyd Norman joined Disney in 1956 and became the studio's first African American animator.

buildup.text: Norman worked on Sleeping Beauty, The Jungle Book, and many other classics alongside Walt Disney himself.

discovery.text: Walt Disney treated Norman as an equal in an era when racial discrimination was widespread in Hollywood.

twist.text: Disney forcibly retired Norman at age 65. He kept showing up to work anyway and was given a desk.

climax.text: Norman continued working into his 80s and became a beloved mentor to new generations of animators.

punchline.text: Disney retired him. He refused to leave and kept drawing.

quiz.question: What made Floyd Norman a pioneer at Disney?
options: He became Disney's first African American animator, working on classics like The Jungle Book
He directed the first Disney sequel

details.summary: Floyd Norman became the first African American animator at Disney in 1956, working on Sleeping Beauty, The Jungle Book, and many other films. His seven-decade career spans the entirety of post-Walt Disney animation history.
details.whyItMatters: Norman's career illuminates both animation's potential for inclusion and the barriers that existed for decades. His persistence through an era of exclusion paved the way for diversity in animation that the industry is still working to achieve.
takeaways: Norman was Disney's first African American animator, hired in 1956
He worked on classics from Sleeping Beauty through modern Disney films
His career spans over seven decades in the animation industry

faq.question: What was Floyd Norman's experience as Disney's first Black animator?
faq.answer: Norman worked directly with Walt Disney on The Jungle Book and was respected for his talent. However, he faced an industry with virtually no other Black creators. His memoir and documentary An Animated Life detail navigating Disney's creative environment as its only Black artist.

faq.question: Is Floyd Norman still working in animation?
faq.answer: Remarkably, yes. Well into his 80s, Norman continues contributing to Disney projects. When Disney tried to retire him, he simply showed up at the studio anyway. His refusal to stop working reflects both his passion and his determination to remain visible.
